subject: Tiered activation & escape-hatch: Sierra Financial readiness and feature backing
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Paul Holt <paul.holt@sierrafin.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Tiered activation request + escape-hatch — Sierra Financial (MVP criteria attached)

Team —

Sierra signed an LOI this morning and procurement asked for a staging plan that guarantees they can go live by mid-Aug if we can commit to the MVP acceptance matrix. Key asks from their security and ops: deterministic routing to a pinned model variant for a subset of traffic, an escape-hatch fallback to a lower-latency generic model if pinned capacity is exhausted, and 30-day telemetry retention for traceability.

They've attached an MVP_criteria doc and a mutual action plan (attached). The commercial ask: if we can scope the gating and escape-hatch and promise a canary in prod within 6 weeks, they will sign the SOW and move to a 12-month reserved capacity commitment.

Can you confirm feasibility and an estimated engineering timeline? If the full deterministic kernel work is too large, would a routing shim + traffic tag be an acceptable interim? We're trying to avoid losing the deal — Sierra's reference would unlock other banking prospects in the region.

Next steps I need by EOD:
- Monica: product tradeoffs and required acceptance criteria tweaks (if any)
- Ben: rough engineering estimate (effort + risk) and suggested workaround
- Karthik: any concerns on committing to the proposed telemetry retention for billing/compliance

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 15 if helpful.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Tiered activation request + escape-hatch — Sierra Financial (MVP criteria attached)

Laura —

Congrats on the LOI. Quick read through the attachments — high-level thoughts:

- Deterministic routing: product-wise this is reasonable as a gated feature for a limited tenant set. We need to define the exact routing semantics (per-customer affinity, percentage of traffic, and what constitutes "exhausted").
- Escape-hatch: functionally straightforward if implemented as a routing policy that falls back to a compatible smaller model; we need SLA language around the fallback behavior so support knows when to escalate.
- Telemetry retention: 30 days is normal for operational traces; for audit-level logs we usually offer 90 days as a paid tier. Is Sierra expecting auditable export for compliance?

I propose the following for an MVP to unblock the commercial team:
1) Routing shim (traffic tags + gateway rule) that pins traffic for 0.5% -> 10% during canary; minimal infra changes.
2) Fallback policy implemented in the routing layer (no kernel changes).
3) Telemetry: grant 30-day trace retention scoped to this tenant with a documented export path to S3 for their auditors.

If Engineering signs off on the shim approach, Product can own the acceptance criteria and playbook (canary steps, rollback, support contacts). Ben — can you confirm the feasibility & effort estimate for the shim + fallback? If that looks acceptable, we'll avoid the full runtime changes for now and put kernel-level deterministic routing on the roadmap after GA.

Laura / Monica —

Thanks for the context. Technical notes and options:

Option A (fast path - recommended for this timeline): routing shim in the gateway that looks for a seat tag (header or JWT claim) and pins those requests to a warmed model container; if capacity is unavailable, route to fallback model and increment a telemetry flag for escalation. Pros: minimal runtime changes, ~2 engineers, 1 sprint to implement + 1 week for canary. Cons: not as deterministic as kernel-level affinity under noisy neighbor conditions.

Option B (longer-term, robust): runtime/kernel deterministic routing with dedicated affinity slots and stricter KV cache pinning. Pros: true determinism under load. Cons: larger effort (4-6 engineer-weeks across runtime + infra), longer QA, potential regressions to performance.

We can deliver Option A as the MVP. Risk: we need to be explicit with Sierra about the "best-effort" nature of the shim under heavy capacity pressure. Also: telemetry export to S3 (30-day retention) is achievable; we'll need a small infra ticket to provision the export bucket and IAM.

I've filed a placeholder ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ENG-7412 (shim-routing MVP) — it lists acceptance criteria and test cases. If Product/Revenue agree to Option A, I estimate a 3-week calendar timeline to canary + rollout.

Ben Carter
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
